title: Night train
text:
The night train from Gdynia to Kraków left at 9.47, and by ten o'clock Jakub had already decided that the old man in his compartment was going to be a problem.

It wasn't anything the man did. He simply sat by the window with a newspaper he wasn't reading, and every few minutes he looked at Jakub over the top of it. He wore a heavy grey coat although the compartment was warm, and his hands, Jakub noticed, were never still – he kept turning a small brass key between his fingers.

Jakub tried to sleep. He had an exam in Kraków at nine the next morning and needed every hour of rest. But each time he closed his eyes, he could feel the man watching him.

At about one in the morning, the train stopped in the middle of nowhere. The lights flickered and went out. In the darkness, Jakub heard the old man stand up.

"Don't be afraid," the man said. His voice was surprisingly gentle. "I only want to ask you something. Are you Jakub Lis? Ewa Lis's son?"

Jakub's heart was beating fast. "How do you know my mother?"

The lights came back on. The old man sat down again, holding the brass key in his open hand as if offering it.

"Forty years ago," he said, "I worked with your grandfather at the shipyard. When I left Poland, in 1981, I left in a hurry, and he kept something for me. A box. He promised to look after it until I came back." He smiled sadly. "I didn't come back for a long time. When I finally did, he had died. I've been looking for your family ever since. I saw your name on your suitcase label."

Jakub stared at the key. He suddenly remembered a small metal box in his mother's wardrobe, with a lock that nobody had ever been able to open. His mother had always called it "Grandad's mystery".

"I think," Jakub said slowly, "my mother has been waiting for you for a very long time."

The train started moving again. Neither of them slept for the rest of the journey, and Jakub, for once, did not think about his exam at all.
